mechanism: From partition-function slopes extract tau(q)=slope-1; score multifractality 0–9 as sum of (1) tau(q) second-difference concavity % negative, (2) deviation of tau(q) from linear random-walk fit via R²/RMSE, (3) peak-to-peak range of first differences of tau(q). Gate MMAR vs GARCH: 7–9 strong MF, 0–2 near monofractal/random walk.
data_needed: Log returns; partition S_q(delta_t) slopes over q grid; discrete d2_tau and d_tau; linregress on tau(q) for q>0.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD 5-minute from Part 1 pipeline context; Python MetaTrader 5 API.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit multifractal-regime applicability sensor that decides whether multifractal volatility models are warranted versus monofractal/GARCH baselines.
quote: Score 7-9: Strongly multifractal. MMAR highly recommended... Score 0-2: Not multifractal. MMAR not recommended, data is too close to a random walk.

mechanism: Estimate global Hurst H via nolds R/S with Anis-Lloyd-Peters correction and RANSAC fit (fallback: find q where tau(q)=0 so H=1/q). H>0.5 persistence (trend-favoring), H<0.5 anti-persistence (mean-reversion), H=0.5 random walk; variance of cumulative returns scales as T^(2H) so mis-set H miscalibrates risk.
data_needed: Return series for hurst_rs; optional tau(q) spline/Brent root for fallback.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD 5-minute returns in series; FBM path illustrations at H=0.3/0.5/0.7.
why_new_for_mis: Operational memory-regime sensor MIS can roll to switch trend vs mean-reversion emphasis and to scale horizon risk beyond naive sqrt(T).
quote: a persistent market (H > 0.5) rewards trend-following strategies, while an anti-persistent market (H < 0.5) rewards mean-reversion strategies.

mechanism: Legendre transform alpha=d(tau)/dq, f(alpha)=alpha*q-tau(q); spectrum width alpha_max-alpha_min measures multifractality (local Hölder heterogeneity); left-skew (longer small-alpha tail) = diverse crash/rough intensities vs uniform calm; peak alpha_0 is dominant regularity. Fit Lognormal/Binomial/Poisson/Gamma cascades by SSE.
data_needed: Discrete tau(q); central differences for alpha; empirical (alpha,f) pairs; theoretical cascade spectra.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: FX like EURUSD cited for moderate widths 0.3–0.5; quiet Asian vs volatile London/news roughness contrast.
why_new_for_mis: Spectrum geometry is a volatility-organization fingerprint—MIS can track width/skew as regime of scaling heterogeneity beyond single H or GARCH variance.
quote: The width of this curve, measured as alpha_max - alpha_min, is a direct measure of multifractality strength.... Most financial time series exhibit slight left-skewness, reflecting the empirical observation that volatility bursts come in a wider range of intensities than quiet periods.

mechanism: Embed two series (shared m, tau), build NxM cross-recurrence matrix CR(i,j)=1 if ||x_i-y_j||<=epsilon; extract CRR (shared state-space overlap), CDET (synchronized sequential evolution), CLAM (asymmetric trapping), CENTR/CDIV/CRATIO over rolling windows (OpenCL batch + CPU line scans). Indicator uses timestamp merge-join + log-return then z-score so epsilon is in SD units.
data_needed: Two aligned OHLC/close series; embDim, delay, epsilon, window, step; optional CRQA_NORM_RETURNS/ZSCORE.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD vs GBPUSD live indicator demo; window default 50; epsilon 0.5 on normalized returns; any chart TF.
why_new_for_mis: Nonlinear inter-instrument coupling/synchronization sensor that correlation cannot give—MIS can detect coupling breakdown as a regime-change cue for pairs/divergence.
quote: When CRR is high, the two series are visiting similar states frequently. When CDET is high, they are not only visiting similar states but doing so in similar sequences.... it is the evolution of those changes that reveals when coupling strengthens, weakens, or breaks down entirely.

mechanism: CSpectrumFitter computes empirical f(α) then fits Normal/Binomial/Poisson/Gamma closed-form spectra via ALGLIB BLEIC under physical bounds; lowest SSE wins and supplies cascade multipliers. On EURUSD M10 50k bars Binomial won (α_min≈0.19, α_max≈0.77) capturing asymmetric steep-left spectrum better than Normal parabola.
data_needed: tau(q), H from partition analysis; BLEIC SSE fits; ENUM_MMAR_DISTRIBUTION params.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_M10; 50,000 bars; partition+spectrum test script.
why_new_for_mis: Turns singularity spectrum into a discrete cascade-type label and parameters—MIS can sense which generative volatility-organization model currently fits the market.
quote: BEST FIT: Binomial (SSE=0.148225, RMSE=0.050553).... The wide gap between α_min and α_max (0.59 units) indicates substantial heterogeneity in the scaling

mechanism: Binary multiplicative cascade draws multipliers M=b^(-V) from fitted Normal/Binomial/Poisson/Gamma, conserves mass per sibling group, integrates measure to theta(t); compose X(t)=B_H[theta(t)] via FBM (Davies-Harte FFT or Cholesky). Steep theta → large returns; flat theta → quiet—volatility clustering without GARCH conditional variance.
data_needed: Fitted H, dist type/params, sample volatility; cascade_b=2, cascade_k; FBM autocovariance gamma(k).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic MMAR paths; validation with H=0.55, k=10 (1024 pts); used later on EURUSD M10.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit trading-time deformation mechanism MIS can use as a generative volatility-cluster prior or to simulate stress paths consistent with observed multifractal structure.
quote: This is the mechanism that generates volatility clustering without any explicit GARCH-like conditional variance.... high-activity periods are bursts where the "market clock" runs fast through the FBM, while quiet periods are stretches where the clock barely advances.

mechanism: CMonteCarlo runs N independent MMAR simulations with adaptive cascade depth k=ceil(log_b(horizon+1)); per-path std of first horizon returns; aggregate mean/median/std and 95% CI via 2.5/97.5 percentiles (distribution-free). Prefer median if heavy-tailed cascades skew the mean.
data_needed: Fitted H, dist params, sample_vol; n_simulations; forecast_horizon bars.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M10; 50,000 bars; horizon 7,200 bars (~50 days M10); 100 sims in test (mean vol 0.000338 vs hist 0.000419).
why_new_for_mis: Forward volatility distribution sensor with honest percentile uncertainty—MIS can size risk from CI width and forecast/historical ratio rather than point GARCH forecasts alone.
quote: The MMAR forecasts a mean volatility of 0.000338 over the next 7,200 bars, which is 19% lower than the historical sample volatility of 0.000419 (ratio = 0.81).

mechanism: CMMAR Fit()/Forecast() facade; article proposes periodic refit to track evolving H, winning cascade distribution, and multifractal score as regime indicators (e.g. H jump 0.48→0.55 = mean-reversion→trend). Demo EURUSD M10: H=0.4817 mild anti-persistence, score 3/9, forecast/hist ratio 0.81 with tight CI.
data_needed: Rolling return windows; Fit status (FITTED vs PARTITION_ONLY); MMARParams H, score, dist; MMARForecast.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD PERIOD_M10; 50k bars; 7200-bar horizon; 1000 simulations; multi-TF comparison suggested.
why_new_for_mis: Packages H + MF score + cascade type + structural vol forecast as a compact regime/change panel MIS can poll on a schedule.
quote: Use the multifractal score and Hurst exponent as regime indicators. A jump from H=0.48 to H=0.55 might signal a shift from mean-reversion to trend-following behavior.

mechanism: Map symbol→currencies→ISO country codes; cache high/optional medium CalendarEventByCountry + CalendarValueHistoryByEvent timestamps; IsNewsWindow (pre mins), IsPostNewsWindow (post mins), IsHighImpactNewsToday (lot-size haircut). Strategy Tester uses CSV from NewsEventLogger with coverage health checks.
data_needed: MQL5 calendar API or NewsCalendarLog_SYMBOL CSV; InpPreEventMins/PostEventMins; importance HIGH/MEDIUM.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD (and GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, USDCAD, XAUUSD, GER40, US30 mappings); demo H1 EMA EA; 2023–2024 CSV verification.
why_new_for_mis: Event-driven volatility/regime gate from the platform calendar—MIS can mark expected liquidity/spread shock intervals without external news scrapers.
quote: Most news filtering strategies focus exclusively on high-impact events, which represent a small fraction of all scheduled releases but account for the majority of intraday volatility spikes.

mechanism: BetSizeBudget yields concurrent long-short imbalance c_t; headroom=1-|c_t| gates new pyramid entries. BetSizeReserve maps imbalance through EF3M mixture CDF; when reserve < open-lots/max_lots, tighten trail by reserve_tighten_mul—senses overcrowding of the active signal book vs historical imbalance distribution.
data_needed: open_t/close_t/sides signal arrays; SeedBudgetMaxima; FitM2N on ≥500 historical c_t; SBridgeConfig thresholds.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Demo BetSizingPyramidEA on PERIOD_H1; synthetic 30-bar illustrations; AFML Part 13 stack.
why_new_for_mis: Portfolio-of-signals occupancy/capacity sensor—MIS can treat book imbalance headroom as a soft liquidity/congestion regime for new risk.
quote: Its complement — 1 − |c_t| — is the available headroom. The bridge checks this before calling TryOpenInitial().... When the reserve drops below the allocation, the trail is tightened

mechanism: CZScore: Z=(close-SMA(N))/population_stddev(N) on closed bars (shift=1); |Z|≥2.5 flags statistically stretched over/undervaluation vs recent vol; exit when Z crosses 0. Adaptive vs fixed RSI/Stoch levels that stay extreme in trends.
data_needed: CopyClose lookback N (default 50); mean and population std; entry sigma input (2.5).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 Strategy Tester Open-prices-only; Ind_ZScore + EA_ZScore_Reversion on PERIOD_CURRENT.
why_new_for_mis: Simple volatility-aware deviation sensor MIS can reuse across symbols/TFs as a stretch/mean-reversion intensity feature without static oscillator bands.
quote: I needed a normalization that measures price deviation from its mean in units of standard deviation.... When the Z-Score deviates and reaches extreme mathematical levels like 2.0 or -2.0, it points to a statistically significant anomaly.

mechanism: COrderBuilder fluent chain validates MqlTradeRequest fields (direction-coupled action/type, SL/TP vs stops level, OrderCheck gate)—order construction API, not market sensing.
why_new_for_mis: Software/API pattern after full read; no MIS sensor.
quote: The fluent builder pattern restructures this process. Instead of assigning struct fields directly, the developer calls self-documenting methods on a builder object in sequence.

mechanism: CObjectPool<T> free-list Acquire/Release O(1) for high-frequency OnCalculate allocations—runtime infrastructure, not market sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: PoolBenchmark on ETHUSD M1 / EURUSD H1 timing demos
quote: The object pool pattern addresses the allocation overhead for this class of workload by front-loading all memory operations into the indicator's initialization phase.

mechanism: IState/CStrategyContext Idle→Entry→InTrade→Exit FSM for EA control flow (MA crossover demo)—software architecture for strategy phases, not market-regime sensing.
why_new_for_mis: EA control-plane pattern; states describe trade lifecycle not market sensors.
